stem:
One way of storing a substance safely is to keep air away from its surface.

Which way of storing a substance does not use this method?

options.text: keeping copper vessels uncovered on a shelf
keeping calcium in a tightly closed bottle of oil

teacher.key_rationale: Sodium (kerosene), white phosphorus (water), and calcium (oil) are all stored under a liquid or sealed cover specifically to keep air/oxygen away because of their reactivity. Copper is unreactive enough to be left uncovered in air, so storing it uncovered does not use the keep-air-away method; C is the odd one out, mirroring the source's sacrificial-metal answer.
